subject: Intermittent VPN route duplication — support ticket #7894
messages:
From: EdgePoint NetOps <netops@edgepoint.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T16:12:00Z
Subject: Intermittent VPN route duplication - support ticket #7894

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

We're seeing duplicated egress flows from our on-prem site to your private deployment over the site-to-site VPN. After a failover on our edge router yesterday evening (10/14), traffic to the Redwood VPC began showing two parallel paths in our telemetry and a burst of SYN retransmits from customer services. We've attached the vpn-state.log and a short pcap summary.

Symptoms observed:
- Two distinct public source IPs for the same internal service flows (appears to be SNAT'd twice)
- Traceroute from our core shows path A (direct tunnel) and path B (via backup transit) both active for overlapping prefixes
- TCP sessions were reset after 10-40s with duplicate SYNs seen on both paths

We suspect a split-horizon BGP propagation combined with NAT policy mismatch on your side or on ours. Can your team confirm whether you have any SNAT rules that would rewrite source IP when the tunnel goes through the backup path? Also, please advise what diagnostic you'd like from our side (iptables-save, traceroute, BGP routes).

Attachments: [vpn-state.log (8.2 KB), pcap-summary.txt (2.1 KB)]

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
NetOps Engineer, EdgePoint Networks
netops@edgepoint.io
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: EdgePoint NetOps <netops@edgepoint.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent VPN route duplication - support ticket #7894

Thanks Liam — adding initial triage notes below and a quick ask for additional artifacts.

What we've done so far (quick checks):
- Checked our VPN health and saw both tunnels up (primary + failover). No obvious crypto key errors.
- Pulled VPC flow logs for the affected service; they show source IPs from two different public SNAT ranges depending on egress node.
- Verified no deliberate BGP announcements from Redwood that would duplicate prefixes.

Hypothesis: split-horizon at EdgePoint + asymmetric path selection causing our edge SNAT to be applied on both legs, leading to two different SNAT translations landing at the same destination and conntrack confusion. If packets from the same TCP session arrive with different source IPs on different egress nodes, conntrack won't match and you'll see resets/duplicate SYNs.

Can you please send:
- output of `iptables -t nat -L -n -v` or equivalent on the edge device for the affected tunnel
- a short BGP neighbor show and route table snapshot around the time of the failover
- confirmation of any recent security-group/firewall changes that restrict ephemeral port ranges

I'll run a quick route and conntrack dump from our side and share. If we confirm conntrack churn, a short-term mitigation is to apply a SNAT-preserve policy (preserve source when forwarding between backup/primary path) or force tunnel affinity.

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Network SRE, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, EdgePoint NetOps <netops@edgepoint.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T20:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent VPN route duplication - support ticket #7894

Adding details from kernel/conntrack side and a quick diagnostic we ran here. Attaching conntrack-dump.txt and route-check.sh output.

Observations from our hosts behind the VPC NAT gateway:
- conntrack entries for the affected sessions show short lifetimes and multiple translations with different src IPs (see conntrack-dump.txt).
- MTU looks consistent end-to-end (1500) so fragmentation isn't the main problem here.
- When we forced traffic to a single egress instance (policy route), sessions are stable.

Quick repro commands we used (feel free to run equivalents on your edge):
- iptables -t nat -S (look for POSTROUTING SNAT rules matched to tunnel interfaces)
- sudo conntrack -L | grep <client-ip> -A 5
- sudo ip route get <dest-ip> via <egress> to confirm symmetric path selection

Short-term mitigation suggestions:
1) On EdgePoint: Add a SNAT bypass for traffic towards the Redwood VPC prefix to preserve original source (if security policy allows).
2) Or: Enforce tunnel stickiness via routing or source-based policy to keep flow on one path.
3) On Redwood: If needed, accept the different source IPs but translate back to a canonical internal IP at the service ingress (more invasive).

I'll coordinate a deeper runbook once we have your iptables and BGP outputs.

Attachments: [conntrack-dump.txt (12 KB), route-check.sh (1.6 KB)]

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Platform Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: EdgePoint NetOps <netops@edgepoint.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent VPN route duplication - support ticket #7894

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Attaching our firewall/SNAT policy and the BGP neighbor dump (edgepoint-sg.txt). Quick summary of our config changes last night:
- We rolled a route-map change that prefers the backup transit for prefixes with prepends (intended to reduce jitter).
- We also tightened our security group to block high ephemeral ports > 49152-65535 by default (we reverted that in the last hour).

From our logs: when failover occurred, the backup path was receiving mirrored flows due to the route-map preference; NAT was applied on both the primary edge and the backup NAT device because we have an outbound SNAT on both devices (we didn't expect overlapping SNAT ranges). That produced two different public source addresses for the same internal socket.

Action we just took:
- Reverted the route-map preference so primary path is preferred again.
- Normalized SNAT pools so backup uses the same SNAT pool as primary (temporary stopgap).

Evidence attached: [edgepoint-sg.txt (4.8 KB)]

Please confirm whether conntrack entries are stabilizing on your side after our changes; we'll keep watch and can schedule a short maintenance window to apply a persistent fix (either stateful synchronization or a single-egress NAT model).

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
NetOps Engineer, EdgePoint Networks
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: EdgePoint NetOps <netops@edgepoint.io>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T23:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent VPN route duplication - support ticket #7894

Appreciate the quick response, Liam and team — this has caused visible customer impact and we're escalating to get a short remediation timeline.

Ask / summary for execs & scheduling:
- Confirmed root cause: split-horizon routing + non-uniform SNAT pools causing asymmetric source translations and conntrack churn.
- Immediate customer impact: intermittent session resets for several paying customers during the failover window (affects API calls and webhooks).
- Short-term actions agreed: EdgePoint reverted the route-map and aligned SNAT pools. Redwood will monitor conntrack stability for 24 hours and provide logs.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Schedule a 1-hour maintenance window on 2026-10-18 02:00-03:00 UTC to implement a persistent solution: either centralized NAT or state-sync between primary/backup NAT devices.
2) Provide customers with a brief incident note and timeline once we have 24h stability confirmation.
3) Create a joint post-mortem and identify where routing policy tests can be added to the pre-prod acceptance criteria.

Please confirm availability for the maintenance window and whether EdgePoint prefers state-sync vs single-egress NAT; we'll coordinate change window and customer comms.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
